## Overview

[PlackettLuce](https://cran.r-project.org/package=PlackettLuce) models the probability
of ranking outcomes and is widely used for farmer-participatory variety trials using
the [tricot](https://tricot.bioversityinternational.org/) approach. `pltree()` extends
this by partitioning trial sites into groups with distinct variety preferences, using
environmental variables as splitting covariates.

This article demonstrates how to:

1. Derive location and date information from a tricot trial dataset.
2. Extract AgERA5 growing-season weather covariates with `ag5_extract()`.
3. Use those covariates in a `pltree()` model.

## Packages

```{r eval = FALSE}
library(ag5Tools)
library(PlackettLuce)
```

## Trial data: `beans`

The `beans` dataset in `PlackettLuce` contains 842 tricot observations from a bean
variety trial in Nicaragua (2015–2016). Each row records which of three randomly
assigned varieties a farmer rated as best and worst.

```{r}
library(PlackettLuce)
data(beans)
str(beans[, c("variety_a", "variety_b", "variety_c",
              "best", "worst", "lon", "lat", "planting_date", "season")])
```

The columns `lon`, `lat`, and `planting_date` give us everything needed to pull
growing-season weather from AgERA5 for each observation.

## Step 1: Derive a date range for each observation

Bean trials in this dataset run approximately 90 days. We add an `end_date` column
from `planting_date + 90`.

```{r}
beans$end_date <- beans$planting_date + 90
range(beans$planting_date)
range(beans$end_date)
```

## Step 2: Extract AgERA5 covariates

We extract two growing-season covariates:

- **Total rainfall** — sum of daily `Precipitation-Flux` (mm) over the growing season.
- **Mean maximum temperature** — mean of daily `Temperature-Air-2m` (Max-24h, °C).

The `ag5_extract()` function accepts a `data.frame` as `coords`. We need to rename
columns to match the expected default names (`lon`, `lat`, `start_date`, `end_date`),
or pass the column names explicitly.

```{r eval = FALSE}
library(ag5Tools)

# Use explicit column names since beans uses 'planting_date' not 'start_date'
precip_list <- ag5_extract(
  coords     = beans,
  lon        = "lon",
  lat        = "lat",
  start_date = "planting_date",
  end_date   = "end_date",
  variable   = "Precipitation-Flux",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data"
)

maxt_list <- ag5_extract(
  coords     = beans,
  lon        = "lon",
  lat        = "lat",
  start_date = "planting_date",
  end_date   = "end_date",
  variable   = "Temperature-Air-2m",
  statistic  = "Max-24h",
  celsius    = TRUE,
  path       = "C:/agera5_data"
)

# Aggregate daily series to trial-level covariates
beans$total_rain <- sapply(precip_list, sum,  na.rm = TRUE)
beans$mean_maxt  <- sapply(maxt_list,  mean, na.rm = TRUE)
```

To download the AgERA5 files for Nicaragua before extracting:

```{r eval = FALSE}
# Nicaragua bounding box: c(north, west, south, east)
ag5_download(
  variable  = "precipitation_flux",
  year      = c(2015, 2016),
  month     = "all",
  day       = "all",
  area      = c(15, -88, 11, -83),
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)

ag5_download(
  variable  = "2m_temperature",
  statistic = "24_hour_maximum",
  year      = c(2015, 2016),
  month     = "all",
  day       = "all",
  area      = c(15, -88, 11, -83),
  path      = "C:/agera5_data"
)
```

## Step 3: Convert rankings to PlackettLuce format

`as.rankings()` converts the tricot best/worst choices into a complete partial ranking
matrix suitable for `PlackettLuce()` and `pltree()`.

```{r eval = FALSE}
# Build a grouped_rankings object from the tricot best/worst format
R <- rank_tricot(data      = beans,
                 items     = c("variety_a", "variety_b", "variety_c"),
                 input     = c("best", "worst"),
                 group     = TRUE)
```

## Step 4: Fit a PlackettLuce tree

`pltree()` uses the environmental covariates to partition the trial sites. Terminal
nodes with meaningfully different worth estimates indicate that variety performance
depends on growing conditions.

```{r eval = FALSE}
pl_tree <- pltree(R ~ total_rain + mean_maxt,
                  data    = beans,
                  minsize = 50)

print(pl_tree)
plot(pl_tree)
```

## Step 5: Inspect worth estimates by node

`itempar()` returns the worth (log-ability) of each variety within each terminal node,
revealing which varieties perform best under wetter or hotter conditions.

```{r eval = FALSE}
itempar(pl_tree)
```

## Adding more covariates

The same workflow extends to any AgERA5 variable. Further covariates commonly used
in variety trial analyses:

| Covariate | AgERA5 variable | Statistic | Aggregation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Growing-season solar radiation | `Solar-Radiation-Flux` | — | sum ÷ 1e6 (MJ/m²) |
| Heat stress days | `Temperature-Air-2m` | `Max-24h` | count days > 35 °C |
| Drought stress days | `Precipitation-Flux` | — | count days < 1 mm |
| Mean vapour pressure | `Vapour-Pressure` | `Mean` | mean (hPa) |

```{r eval = FALSE}
radn_list <- ag5_extract(
  coords     = beans,
  lon        = "lon",
  lat        = "lat",
  start_date = "planting_date",
  end_date   = "end_date",
  variable   = "Solar-Radiation-Flux",
  path       = "C:/agera5_data"
)

beans$total_radn <- sapply(radn_list, sum, na.rm = TRUE) / 1e6  # MJ/m²

pl_tree2 <- pltree(R ~ total_rain + mean_maxt + total_radn,
                   data    = beans,
                   minsize = 50)
plot(pl_tree2)
```
